Rugged Phone or Rugged Tablet: Which Do You Need?

13 October 2026 Tuga Hardware

If the device will come out of a pocket all day for a photo, a message, a fault code or a parts label, buy the handheld. On Android that is the Tuga A6 at £349. If the screen is doing the work, which means long forms, drawings, quotes walked through at a kitchen table or a spreadsheet, buy a tablet: the Tuga A8 at £379 if you need to hold it in one hand, the Tuga A10 at £449 if you need to read a plan without zooming.

That is the short answer. The harder question is whether you need one device or two. It is easy to buy a tablet, keep using your personal phone for everything else, and end up with the tablet in the van and the phone doing the job. It is just as easy to buy a handheld and spend the year squinting at a form built for a desktop. Getting the shape right matters more than any single spec.

What We Mean by Rugged Phone

A rugged phone is a pocket sized device for site work: something that takes photos in bad light and survives knocks, drops and weather. The A6 is the Tuga Android handheld in that size class (the Windows WH6 is covered below). It is a 6 inch Android 15 handheld with dual SIM 4G, dual-band Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.1 and NFC, sealed to IP67 and rated for 1.5 metre drops, with a built-in 2D barcode scanner.

The A6 is a handheld with 4G. If making and taking calls on the device matters to you, ask us before you order.

The Screen Question

Screen size is the one thing you cannot change later, so start there. Three sizes, three different jobs.

6 Inches: The A6

The A6 screen is 2160 x 1080 FHD+, sharper than either tablet on paper. Physical size is the issue, not sharpness. An app built for a phone is comfortable on 6 inches. A PDF drawing, a desktop web app with a sidebar, or a form with dozens of fields is not. You can, with pinching and scrolling, but not all day.

8 Inches: The A8

The A8 screen is 1280 x 800 and runs at 1000 nits, against 350 on the A10. The A6 does not list a brightness figure. Eight inches is the size at which a long form, a route or a quote with pictures becomes readable without zooming, and it is still small enough to hold in one hand on a ladder or drop into a van door pocket.

10.1 Inches: The A10

The A10 screen is 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200, Full HD. This is the one for drawings, BIM viewers, full spreadsheets and PDF plans, where you need the whole page at once. The catch is brightness. The A10 is rated at 350 nits against 1000 on the A8, so it is at its best in a cab, a site office or under cover rather than on an open roof in July. If most of your reading happens in direct sun, the A8 is the better outdoor screen even though it is smaller.

The Pocket Question

The A6 weighs 277g and the A10 680g. No weight is listed for the A8. What matters is where the device lives. A handheld goes in a pocket or a belt holster, and it is still there when you climb into a loft or lean over a trench. A tablet lives in the van, on a dashboard mount, in a bag or in your hand. When you need both hands for a parcel or a ladder, a tablet has to be put down somewhere, which is an extra risk for any device.

The accessories follow the shape. For the A6: the Belt Holster at £22 and the Car Phone Mount at £17. For the A8 and A10: the Vehicle Mounting Dock at £109 for the dashboard (the A8 has VESA mount points on the back for it), plus the Charging Dock at £49.99 for the A10 in the office or workshop. The A6 and A10 come with a hand strap in the box; for the A8, the Hand Strap is £24. The 12V DC Car Charger at £26 fits every device in the range. The full list is on our accessories page.

Specs That Are Not About Size

The smallest device is not simply a cut down tablet. It wins on some specs and gives ground on others.

  • Barcode scanning. The A6 has a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys. Neither tablet has one, so on the A8 or A10 you are relying on a camera scanning app. If you scan parts, stock or delivery labels every day, this alone can decide it.
  • Camera. All three have a 13MP rear camera with a flash and a 5MP front camera, and the A8's rear camera is listed as autofocus. For fuse boards, voids and lofts, the flash helps.
  • Connectivity. All three have 4G and take two SIMs, so you can carry two networks for patchy rural coverage. On the A6 the second SIM slot is shared with the microSD card, so it is one or the other.
  • Battery. The A6 has a 5050mAh battery, the A8 8000mAh, the A10 8000mAh with quick charge. The A6 and A8 batteries are removable, so a charged spare can take over mid shift. The A10's is not listed as removable.
  • Memory and storage. The A6 has 4GB of RAM and 64GB of storage, expandable by microSD up to 256GB. The A8 has 6GB and 128GB with a microSD slot, and the A10 8GB and 128GB, expandable to 2TB. If you run heavy apps or keep a lot of photos on the device, the tablets have more headroom.
  • Operating system. The A6 runs Android 15, the A10 Android 14 and the A8 Android 12, the oldest of the three. Check that the apps you rely on support it before you choose the A8.
  • Sealing. The A10 is IP68 and MIL-STD-810H. The A6 is IP67 and rated for 1.5 metre drops. The A8 is IP67, with no drop rating listed. None of the three is rated IP69K, so none should be pressure washed. Our IP ratings guide explains the difference.
  • Gloves. None of the three lists glove mode, though the A6 scan keys work with gloves on. No fingerprint sensor or face unlock is listed on any of the three, so plan on a PIN.
  • Ports. The A8 has USB-C, a DC input and pogo pin contacts. The A10 has USB-C, a pogo pin connector for docking and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The A6 has USB-C and charging contacts for a dock. No USB-A port is listed for any of the three, so a USB-A peripheral needs the USB-C to USB-A OTG Adapter at £8.
  • Operating temperature. The A10 is rated to operate from -20°C to 60°C, the A6 from -20°C to 50°C. No operating temperature is listed for the A8.

A tablet costs you more than pocket size. Against the A6 you give up the built-in barcode scanner and 277g in a pocket, plus the A6's listed 1.5m drop rating if you pick the A8 (which lists none), and its removable battery if you pick the A10. In return you get screen size, more RAM, double the storage and a bigger battery, with 1000 nit brightness and a removable battery on the A8, and IP68, MIL-STD-810H and dual SIM alongside a microSD card on the A10. A fair trade if the screen is what you need. A poor one if it is not.

One Device or Two?

This is the real decision. There are three ways to set it up.

One Handheld for Work

The A6 at £349 is the lowest priced device in our range and the one built to live in a pocket, so it is the one to consider if you want one pocketable work device rather than a tablet that stays in the van. If you want it to replace your personal phone, ask us about calling first. If your job sheets, invoices, photos and messages all live in phone apps, you may never miss the bigger screen. This may suit sole traders doing domestic work, delivery drivers and anyone on their feet all day.

One Tablet Plus the Phone You Already Have

If you are happy with your personal phone for calls and messages and simply need a work screen that survives site, buy the A8 or A10 and leave the phone in your pocket. This suits electricians filling in test schedules, surveyors and site managers reading plans, and field service engineers running a job queue from a vehicle mount. The weak point is that your personal phone is then doing the site photos.

A Handheld and a Tablet

A small firm could run both: an A6 for each person who is in and out of properties, and an A8 or A10 in the van or with whoever does the quoting. An A6 and an A8 together come to £728 before any discount, an A6 and an A10 to £798. Two or more devices on one order get 3% off automatically, rising to 5% at three or four devices, 8% at five to nine and 10% at ten or more. The discount applies to devices only. Our bulk orders page has the detail.

The cost comparison worth doing is one rugged device against a consumer tablet and phone that may need replacing after a hard knock. Our cost comparison guide walks through the tablet case.

If You Need Windows

Everything above is about the Android range, because if your software runs in a browser or an app, Android is usually enough. If one program you rely on only runs on a Windows PC, the same question exists on the Windows side: the Tuga WH6 is a 6.5 inch handheld at £699, the Tuga W8 an 8 inch tablet at £629 and the Tuga W10 a 10.1 inch tablet at £649, all running Windows 11. Our Android or Windows guide has a quick test to tell you which side you are on.

Which One for Your Work

  • On your feet, in and out of properties or a cab all day, app based paperwork: Tuga A6, £349.
  • Forms with many fields, quotes with pictures, one hand on a ladder, bright light: Tuga A8, £379.
  • Drawings, plans, spreadsheets, BIM viewers, mostly under cover or in a vehicle: Tuga A10, £449.
  • Photos in dark spaces are the main job: any of the three, since the A6, A8 and A10 all have a flash on the 13MP rear camera. Pick between them on screen size.
  • Barcodes every day: the Tuga A6, which has a built-in 2D scanner, at £349.
  • Barcodes or QR codes now and then: a camera scanning app on a tablet may be enough, but test your own app on the device first. Our barcode scanner guide covers when a built in scan engine is worth paying for.

Whichever you choose, check your own apps on the device rather than assuming. A job management app that works on a phone may lay out badly on a tablet, and a desktop web app may be unusable on a 6 inch screen. If you are still unsure, our four question picker narrows it down, or email us what you do and we will point you at one device.

Buying

Every device comes with a 12 month warranty. The paid 3-Year Warranty is offered on every model: £65 on the A6, A8 and A10, £79 on the W8 and W10, and £89 on the WH6. Delivery is free to UK addresses and takes 7 to 10 working days, and you have 30 days from delivery to return a device in its original condition and packaging. Prices are what you pay. No VAT to add.
